title: Highlights vs Florida || Wisconsin Volleyball || Sept. 2, 2026
snapshotDescription:
The No. 5 Wisconsin volleyball team defeated No. 17 Florida (25-21, 20-25, 25-19, 24-26, 15-13) in a five-set battle at the UW Field House, picking up its first home win of the 2026 season in front of a sold-out crowd.

Audrey Flanagan led the Badgers with a career-high 18 kills, Grace Egan added a season-high 17, and Lynney Tarnow had 16 kills on a .429 hitting percentage. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer dished out a season-high 55 assists and 15 digs, and libero Anna Bardaro had a team-high 19 digs.

It was Wisconsin's first win over the Gators in the Field House in program history.

recap: By: Molly Sheehan MADISON, Wis. — The No. 5 Wisconsin volleyball team defeated No. 17 Florida (25-21, 20-25, 25-19, 24-26, 15-13) in a five-set battle to pick up its first home win of the 2026 season in front of a sold out crowd Wednesday night. Outside hitter Audrey Flanagan led the Badgers (2-3) with a career-high 18 kills, chipping in nine digs and three blocks in the process. Rightside Grace Egan added a season-high 17 kills of her own, as middle blocker Lynney Tarnow added 16 kills of her own off a .429 hitting percentage while adding five blocks. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer dished out a season-high 55 assists and 15 digs, good for a double-double. Libero Anna Bardaro paced the backcourt, contributing a team-high 19 digs. The match opened in a back-and-forth battle before a 4-0 scoring run in the middle of the set, capped off by a pair of kills from Flanagan. Wisconsin continued to build momentum late into the set behind kills from freshman Kymora Scott and Eva Travis before Tarnow sealed the 25-21 set victory with a kill of her own. The middle blocker posted four kills in the first set, leading the team to an overall hitting percentage of .312. ALL-OUT EFFORT FROM EVA! Today's smart play, presented by @ATCgrid #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/haz6xdLGl3 — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 3, 2026 Kymora with a SPARK! #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/hawNa57eei — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 3, 2026 The second set opened similarly, with Fuerbringer providing an ace before the Gators provided an answer of their own. The opponent's offense came out strong in the frame, holding Wisconsin to a .189 hitting percentage (12 - 5 - 37), to take the second set 25-20. Egan provided a spark early in the third set with a pair of kills to add to a 3-0 run. The senior later went on a 4-1 scoring run alone to help build the lead. A strong hitting performance helped Wisconsin to 15 kills in the set, with a pair from Flanagan capping the set off with a victory, 25-19, and go up two sets to one. BACK-TO-BACK POINTS FROM EGAN! 🤩 #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/44RAzgs9Dk — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 3, 2026 Florida opened the fourth set with a 5-0 run, but the Badgers brought the set close with a late 5-0 run of their own. The two teams traded points late, before a bad set gave the Gators the set win. The Badgers set the tone in the fifth with a 6-1 burst thanks to back-to-back kills from Scott. Florida mounted another late 3-0 push to tie the set at 13 apiece, but a Flanagan kill helped seal the victory over the Gators with a 15-13 final in set five. With the five-set victory, Wisconsin completed its first home win of the season, picking up its first win against the Gators at the Field House in program history. Straight from the Court: Head Coach Kelly Sheffield (on the victory): "I thought we battled, we fought, we scratched and we challenged a lot of you players at different times in the match." Freshman Lynney Tarnow (on a home victory) "I've been waiting to play in the Field House for so long now, so I think just the energy and feeling the crowd having our backs and the support through a five-setter was such a cool feeling." Freshman Kymora Scott (on starting tonight) "I just felt ready and excited to be out there. When things started picking up for me I was definitely excited. I was excited coming in to support my teammates, but it's always fun having your moment." Notes: The five-set thriller of a victory over the No. 17 Florida Gators marks the first match Wisconsin has won over the Gators in the UW Field House. The Badgers were previously 0-3. Last year's victory against the Gators was at the Kohl Center. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer recorded her 19th double-double of her career, and second of the season with a 55 assist, 15 dig performance against the Gators. Freshman Kymora Scott got her first collegiate start at middle blocker. Scott totaled seven kills on 16 swings for a .312 (7-2-16) hitting percentage. Wisconsin had three players with double-figure kills; Audrey Flanagan (18), Lynney Tarnow (16), and Grace Egan (17). The 18 and 17 kills for Flanagan and Egan were also season-highs. Freshman Lynney Tarnow collected a career-best 16 kills against Florida. She also had a personal-best five blocks. Libero Anna Bardaro has now tallied double-figure digs in the last four matches. She totaled 19, matching a career-best last dig against Stanford on Aug. 30. Up Next: Wisconsin returns to the Field House against Auburn on Thursday, Sept. 3, to wrap up Big Ten/SEC Challenge week competition. First serve is slated for 7 p.m. with the match airing on FS1.

recap: By: Molly Sheehan MADISON, Wis. — The No. 5 Wisconsin volleyball team (3-3) cruised past Auburn (3-2) in straight sets (25-23, 25-17, 25-20) at the Field House on Thursday night. Freshman Halle Thompson led the way for Wisconsin with 11 kills and 11 digs, good for her first career double-double. Senior Eva Travis added 10 kills of her own, as Natalie Wardlow pitched in eight. Junior Charlie Fuerbringer continued to be a staple at setter, adding 35 assists and 12 digs to combine for her 20th career double-double. The Badgers came out firing right away, opening the set with a dominant 4-0 showing. Bardaro went to work from the service line, tallying her first ace of the match to cap off the early scoring run. Auburn charged back late in the set with a 4-0 scoring run of their own to bring the set level, 23-23, before a service error and kill from Flanagan sealed the first set win. It was a back-and-forth affair to open the second frame. The Badgers found some separation in the middle of the set with the help of a 7-0 run, which featured kills from Tarnow and Thompson alongside a Badger block. Halle going to WORK! ⭐ #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/xkMgVpLkdC — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 4, 2026 Wisconsin sealed the second set win in dominant fashion, embarking on a 13-4 run that was helped by Bardaro serving in a 7-0 run. Alongside the strong serving, the Badgers posted a season-high hitting percentage in the frame alone at .517 (18 - 3 - 29). Eva tacks on another kill! 🔨 #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/hCMd8RXwrY — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 4, 2026 After trading points to open the third set, Auburn provided a response in the latter half of the set to hold a 17-16 lead late in the frame. UW provided an answer however, rattling off four straight points thanks to three kills from Travis and a block from Tarnow. From there, the Badgers cruised to their first home sweep of the season off a final Thompson kill. Natalie came to play ‼️ #OnWisconsin pic.twitter.com/bfmvEug7C2 — Wisconsin Volleyball (@BadgerVB) September 4, 2026 With the win, the Badgers stand 1-0 all-time against the Tigers and improve to 2-0 at the Field House this season. Straight from the Court: Head Coach Kelly Sheffield (on Halle Thompson's performance) "I thought she was not just aggressive, but I thought offensively she was, she was smart. We gave her the ball an awful lot…Halle's like a double shot of espresso. I wanted to make sure that we weren't sleepy out there and the building wasn't sleepy and I think people are excited to see her play. I know she was excited to see her play…. I just think she was really, really revved up tonight but we needed her. We needed those swings." (on the team's discipline) "We didn't get tooled, we didn't get used very much and when you got, when you're playing against somebody with speed, it's really easy to, for these wipe off shots and be chipped off the block. We were really disciplined with our hands. Our backcourt was just flying all over the place. So, we kept the ball off the ground, we controlled the ball, and then we worked in transition, and Charlie found our attackers, and you know, they were working hard in transition. A lot of our middle kills were transition" Natalie Wardlow (on her mindset) "My mindset is always on how can I be good for the team and not getting so into myself. Kelly always talks about finding those opportunities or just being ready to go in, and I think also tonight, just being there for my team and just making smart decisions." Eva Travis (on the team's connection) "Coming to a new team is never easy for anyone, but working in practice every day has helped a lot of us just to create our bond and our connection better." Notes: Thursday's 3-0 win over Auburn marks the first win over the Tigers in program history. The two had previously not met. Freshman Halle Thompson hit a career-best 11 kills on 30 attempts. Thompson has tallied her first-career double-double with 11 kills and 11 digs. The Badgers had four players with double-figure dig totals. Anna Bardaro had a match-high 17 digs, Charlie Fuerbringer totaled 12, while Kristen Simon and Thompson had 11. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer recorded her 20th-career double-double with a 36 assist, 11 dig performance. This marks back-to-back matches with a double-double. The Badgers hit .305 (46-14-105), marking the second time this season where the team hit .300 or better. The last time Wisconsin hit .300 or better was on Aug. 22 over No. 7 Louisville when the team hit .327. Up Next: Wisconsin heads south to take on No. 12 Texas A&M on Friday, Sept. 11. First serve is slated for 8 p.m., with the match airing on SEC ESPN Network. recap: By: Molly Sheehan MADISON, Wis. — The No. 6 Wisconsin volleyball team defeated the Marquette Golden Eagles in four sets (22-25, 25-17, 25-19, 25-15) on Thursday evening at the UW Field House. Freshman Decelise Champion paved the way for Wisconsin with her first career double-double on a career-high 20 kills and 11 digs, also turning in three blocks. Freshman Audrey Flanagan added 13 kills and a trio of Badgers in Lynney Tarnow , Jaela Auguste and Eva Travis tallied 10 kills each. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer continued to provide steadiness, chipping in 54 assists and six digs. Libero Anna Bardaro contributed 16 digs, her seventh double-figure total this season. The match opened in back-and-forth fashion as both teams traded points before a 5-0 burst from Marquette forced the Badgers into a timeout. Wisconsin claimed the next two points off a kill from Auguste and an ace from Isabelle Hoppe before later putting together a 6-1 run. Another late 3-0 burst from Wisconsin leveled the score 20-20, but Marquette claimed four of the last five rallies to grab the first set win, 25-22. Wisconsin found a quick response in the second set, finding three separate 3-0 runs to help cruise to a 25-17 set victory. Champion helped spark two of those runs with kills, ending the set with a seven-kill performance on a hitting percentage of .778 (7 - 0 - 9) in the set alone. UW maintained its momentum in the third set, sparking a 6-0 to take a six point advantage into the media timeout. In that span, Flanagan put together a strong performance from the service line, posting a service ace as Auguste and Travis each turned in a kill of their own. From there, the Badgers saw another strong hitting performance from Champion and Flanagan. Champion turned in four more kills as Flanagan tallied another ace. Marquette provided a late answer, but Wisconsin won the last two rallies to seal the third set and take a 2-1 advantage into the fourth. Flanagan continued to find a spark in the fourth set, tallying six kills in the frame. The two teams traded points to hold the score close, 16-14, before the Badgers went on a 9-1 run to seal the match win. Straight from the Court: Head Coach Kelly Sheffield (on the first-set comeback): "Even when your best player or one of your best attackers is not on top of their game, there's enough talent in here where everybody else can kind of steady the boat and that's the goal. The goal is to be a great team, be resilient when things aren't going well, and lean on each other." (on the team's progress this season) "We're getting better every week. Certainly having Decelise and her size up there can make a difference as well. But across the board, I think we're understanding, we're getting cleaner feet and our hands, we're lining up a lot better. We're heading in the right direction." Senior Eva Travis (on the Badgers' multiple attacking threats): "We have so many weapons on our team. Charlie spreads us out a lot, which gives us one blocker a lot and that's why we're able to put up these numbers. It's just so fun to be able to rely on each other." Notes: Wisconsin improves to 26-1 all-time against the Marquette Golden Eagles, and 14-1 when playing in Madison. With the win, the Badgers improve to 92-8 (.920) when playing at the UW Field House since 2020. The Badgers totaled 64 kills in the four sets, setting a new season-high. UW had five players who achieved double-figure kill totals in the four-set match over Marquette. Decelise Champion led all with 20, while freshman Audrey Flanagan added 13, and Jaela Auguste , Eva Travis and Lynney Tarnow tallied 10 each. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer dished out 54, one shy of her season-best of 55 against Florida on September 2. After missing the last five matches, middle blocker Jaela Auguste achieved a 10 kill, three block stat line. In her first match in the Field House, freshman Decelise Champion had a career and match high 20 kills, 11 digs, three blocks, and clipped a .441 (20-5-34) hitting percentage. Wisconsin clipped a .369 hitting percentage, a new season-high. With 16 digs, libero Anna Bardaro tallied her seventh match with a double-digit dig total. Up Next: Wisconsin returns to the UW Field House to take on in-state rival Milwaukee on Friday, Sept. 18. First serve is set for 7 p.m. with the match airing on B1G+. recap: By: Molly Sheehan MADISON, Wis. — The No. 6 Wisconsin volleyball team defeated the Milwaukee Panthers in four sets (25-18, 25-18, 22-25, 25-15) to wrap up non-conference play at the UW Field House on Friday night. Freshman Kymora Scott led the Badgers with a career-high 13 kills on a .579 hitting percentage, also chipping in three blocks. Senior Grace Lopez chipped a double-double with 11 kills and 11 digs, as Eva Travis and Natalie Wardlow added eight apiece. Senior Charlie Fuerbringer tallied her sixth double-double of the season with a 54 assist, 16 dig performance. Libero Anna Bardaro added a team-high 17 digs, chipping in three aces from the service line. A pair of 3-0 runs early in the first set helped Wisconsin to build separation. The Badgers claimed the last eight of nine rallies helped by three kills in a row from Champion to claim the first set, 25-18. Wisconsin continued the momentum into the second set, opening the frame with a 7-2 run to force a Milwaukee timeout. From there, the Badgers found another 4-0 burst off a trio of kills and an ace turned in by Fuerbringer before Halle Thompson sealed the set with a kill, 25-18. Scott provided consistency in the frame, turning in four kills on four attempts. The third set opened in similar fashion before Milwaukee mounted a late push, securing the last three rallies to win the set 25-22. The Badgers found a quick answer in the fourth set thanks to back-to-back service aces from Bardaro. Travis and Scott combined for three kills under a 3-0 serving run from junior Morgan Van Wie to close out the frame, helping lift Wisconsin to victory. With the win, the Badgers hold to a 4-0 record at the Field House heading into conference play, picking up its 28th win over the Panthers in the process. Wisconsin finished with a hitting percentage of .326 (66-20-141), its second consecutive performance above the .300 mark. Straight from the Court: Head Coach Kelly Sheffield (on where the team is at): "It's a roller coaster. There's a lot of learning. The potential is great, we've had some great wins, some extremely great moments. They're learning to dig in — they've got a ways to go to learn to dig in." Notes: Wisconsin improves to 28-5 all-time and 19-2 in Madison against the Panthers with the 3-1 victory. For a second night in a row, the Badgers clipped a .300 or better hitting percentage. Wisconsin hit .326 compared to MKE's .210. Freshman Alyssa Konrad saw time on the court against the Panthers. Konrad served as a serving specialist primarily. Setter Charlie Fuerbringer recorded her sixth double-double of the season, 23rd of her career, with a 54 assist, 16 dig performance. Also recording a double-double was Grace Lopez , her 18th of her career, and first since December 6, 2024 against SDSU. Lopez tallied 11 kills and 11 digs. With 13 kills and three blocks, freshman middle Kymora Scott set new career-highs. Wisconsin finishes the non-conference portion of their schedule 6-4. Up Next: Wisconsin opens conference play for Steve Lowe Night against No. 25 Oregon at the UW Field House on Thursday, Sept. 24. First serve is set for 7 p.m. with the match airing on B1G+. Travis and Champion led the way, tallying three apiece early as the Badger Block chipped in three points in the frame. Purdue (8-3, 1-1) combined for a late 3-0 push to cut Wisconsin's lead down to four, but the Badgers swiftly responded with a triad of kills from Fuerbringer, Champion and Travis before a Champion kill sealed the set, 25-18. title: Highlights vs Eastern Michigan || Wisconsin Football || Sept. 19, 2026
snapshotDescription:
The Wisconsin Badgers earned a 54-10 win over Eastern Michigan inside Camp Randall Stadium. An explosive first half on offense and three forced turnovers fueled Wisconsin, which led 31-7 at halftime.

Quarterback Colton Joseph threw a program-record 302 first-half passing yards and finished with 408 total yards and four total touchdowns, including his first rushing score of the season. Tyrell Henry set a school record with 14 receptions for 160 yards and a touchdown, and Jacob Harris had a career-high 89 receiving yards.

Mason Posa grabbed his first career interception, Matt Jung had an interception, a pass breakup and a quarterback hurry, and Cooper Catalano recovered a fumble for a touchdown. Gavin Lahm was 6-for-6 on extra points with two field goals.

title: Highlights at Penn State || Wisconsin Football || Sept. 26, 2026
snapshotDescription:
The Wisconsin Badgers completed a 17-point comeback to defeat No. 13 Penn State, 24-20, at Beaver Stadium on Saturday night. Colton Joseph threw two touchdown passes in the final 3:31 of play to propel the Badgers to their largest road comeback since 2001. UW has now won 3 of its last 4 games against ranked opponents, dating back to last season.

Joseph ended the night with 235 passing yards and three touchdowns, including a rushing score. Harris had a team-high five receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown, while RB Darrion Dupree posted 52 yards on the ground. 

LB Mason Posa paced the defense with 12 tackles (8 solo) and one tackle for a loss. Perkins caught his first career interception, and the first by a Badger defensive lineman since 2018. DL Hammond Russell IV caused chaos up front with a pass breakup, 1.5 sacks, and 1.5 tackles for losses.

Up Next: UW returns to Camp Randall on Saturday, Oct. 3 to host Michigan State for Homecoming. Kickoff against the Spartans is scheduled for 11:30 a.m. CT, with the game airing on Big Ten Network.
